en: Points of Controversy:
The Refutation Section,
Chapter Sixteen.
The Discourse on Encouragement:
Does one person encourage the mind of another? Yes.
Does one person exert another’s mind, thinking, “May you not be lustful,” “may you not be hateful,” “may you not be deluded,” or “may you not be defiled”?
One should certainly not say so...
[and so on] ... Does one person exert another’s mind?
Yes.
One person generates in another the wholesome root of non-greed … the wholesome root of non-hatred …
He generates the wholesome root of non-delusion;
he generates faith;
he generates energy.
Does it generate mindfulness … does it generate concentration … does it generate wisdom?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … “Does one person uplift the mind of another? Yes.
Does one exert oneself so that the contact arisen in another “may not cease”?
One should certainly not say so …pe… [and likewise for] the feeling arisen in another …pe…
Does one exert wisdom that has arisen with the thought, “May it not cease”?
One should certainly not say so … [and so on] … Does one person exert another’s mind?
“Yes.
“Another abandons lust for the sake of another; he abandons hatred for the sake of another.”
“He abandons delusion” … [and so on] … “he abandons lack of moral dread”?
One should not say this … [and so on] …
Does one person uplift the mind of another?
Yes. Does one person develop the path for the sake of another? ... [Yes].
"One develops the foundation of mindfulness...
[and so on] ...one develops the factor of enlightenment"?
One should not say this... [and so on].
Does one person uplift the mind of another?
Yes. Does one person fully understand suffering for the sake of another? ... [and so on] ... Yes.
“Does one develop the path?
“One should not say so…” [and so on].
“Does one person exert another’s mind? [One should not say so.]
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then one person is the doer for another; that is, another makes happiness or suffering, and another experiences it?
You must not say so… [and so on].
"One person exerts the mind of another"?
Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
“Evil is done by oneself alone … [as before] … No one can purify another.
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes, [it is so].
Therefore, it should not be said that one person can uplift the mind of another.
Is it not to be said that one person can uplift the mind of another?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that there are those who have attained strength and there are those who have attained mastery? Yes, they exist.
Since there are those who have attained strength and those who have attained mastery, then indeed, O friend, you must admit this: [that there is a distinction between them].
"One person uplifts the mind of another.
The Discussion on Uplifting is finished.
